holidays.name: National Gingerbread Day
holidays.description: A spicy-sweet day for bakers and cookie fans to whip up gingerbread cookies, cakes, and even little houses, no matter how far from Christmas it is.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it grew out of food-calendar traditions and baking enthusiasts rather than an official proclamation. Gingerbread itself dates back to medieval Europe, where it was a popular fair treat.
holidays.funFact: Queen Elizabeth I of England is said to have had gingerbread cookies made in the likeness of her visiting dignitaries.

holidays.name: World Environment Day
holidays.description: The biggest global day for encouraging environmental action, with cleanups, tree plantings, and campaigns that have everyone suddenly very concerned about their plastic straws.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1972 on the opening day of the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment. It has been celebrated every year since 1974.
holidays.funFact: Each year a different country hosts the celebrations and a different theme is chosen, from wildlife crime to beating plastic pollution.

holidays.name: Festival of Popular Delusions Day (Veggie Pride Parade Season Kickoff)
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek nod to quirky belief and mass enthusiasm, an excuse to ponder the wacky ideas people have latched onto throughout history.
holidays.origin: Inspired by Charles Mackay's 1841 book 'Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds,' which chronicled tulip mania and other historical crazes. The date is an informal, unofficial observance among trivia fans.
holidays.funFact: At the peak of Dutch tulip mania in the 1630s, a single rare bulb reportedly sold for more than the price of a fancy canal house, though historians now debate how extreme the craze really was.

holidays.name: National Ketchup Day
holidays.description: A salute to the red condiment that sits on every diner table, with fries, burgers, and brave scrambled eggs all invited to the party.
holidays.origin: Ketchup began as a fermented fish sauce called ke-tsiap in Southeast China. British traders brought it west, and tomatoes were added in the early 1800s in America. The day is an unofficial food observance celebrated by condiment fans.
holidays.funFact: In the 1830s, tomato ketchup was sold as a medicine, and it was marketed as a cure for indigestion.

holidays.name: Hot Air Balloon Day
holidays.description: A day to look to the skies and celebrate the colorful, floating wonder of hot air ballooning, the world's gentlest form of aerial adventure.
holidays.origin: It commemorates June 5, 1783, when the Montgolfier brothers publicly demonstrated their first hot air balloon in Annonay, France, before a crowd of astonished onlookers.
holidays.funFact: The first passengers in a Montgolfier balloon later in 1783 were a sheep, a duck, and a rooster, who landed safely and became very unlikely aviation pioneers.
